subject: Behind every revolutionary new technology promising to replace human labor is the tedious human labor that makes it possible
posts:
The digital revolution wasn't built on code alone; it was built on the backs of invisible workers in cafeterias and prisons. A necessary look at the human cost of 'innovation'.

The Information Wage
Evidence: tech progress, hidden human labor, systemic extraction
#History #Labor

The tech industry claims that automation is a clean, revolutionary process that eliminates the need for tedious human labor, creating a more efficient future.
Stated Judgement: (+0.5, +1.0) — Innovative Neutral

The reality is that 'automation' often just hides the human labor, moving it to precarious, low-wage, or incarcerated populations to maintain the illusion of machine-only efficiency.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.5, -1.0) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Reckoning.
The narrative of 'revolutionary' tech is a bait-and-switch that erases the human labor required to train and maintain the systems, leading to systemic exploitation.

The article explores the history of data entry, from the 1970s to the present, highlighting how corporations have consistently relied on marginalized labor to digitize the world, often under poor conditions.

The Poison:
The persistent dehumanization of data workers, comparing them to prisoners or assembly-line cogs, reveals a deep-seated contempt for the labor that makes the digital economy possible.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error is in the WHY. The industry claims the goal is 'efficiency' (HOW), but the actual effect is the extraction of value from vulnerable populations (WHO) to keep costs artificially low.

Social Physics Analysis:
This is a clear case of anti-social power. Corporations use the pretext of 'technological progress' to justify the exploitation of invisible labor, projecting the image of a 'clean' digital future.

The Trajectory: The Path of Reckoning.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a trajectory toward Greater Evil. The system relies on the active suppression of the human cost to function.

The Unavoidable Truth: No technology is truly autonomous; it is always supported by a hidden layer of human effort.

The Unavoidable Lie: That the digital revolution is a purely mechanical advancement.

Alethekanon:
The history of data entry is the history of the industrialization of the mind. By treating human cognition as a commodity to be keyed into a disk, we have systematically devalued the very labor that powers our modern world.

Awwthekanon:
It breaks my heart to think of all the people whose hard work was hidden away and treated as if it didn't matter. Every person deserves to be seen and valued for their contribution, not just used as a tool.

Brothekanon:
So the 'AI revolution' is just the 1970s with better branding? We're still just cramming people into rooms to do the boring stuff so the tech bros can claim they 'invented' intelligence. Same old story, just faster internet.
